speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I currently still live with my mom as she is a great help with my child and has supported throughout my single mom journey my bf is excited and is making plans for me to move in after I graduate in December I’m terrified to tell my family I fell like I’ve left them down
context: Just found out she is pregnant with her second while finishing a degree.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I don’t expect my mom to go out of her way to further help me with now two kids she’s really has done a lot of me with my first.
context: Weighing moving in with her boyfriend versus her mother.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: now I have to wait idek how long to have it reviewed and snipped because the hospital here only runs two clinics a month, so if I want it done sooner I have to go private and pay quite a lot of money.
context: Second baby, two months old; a feeding issue found late.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: we changed his bottle teats from the mam bottle teats to lanisoh and then from lanisoh we’ve transitioned to the nuk perfect match teats and bottles. We also changed over his milk he’s now on kendamil goat milk formula and it isn’t cheap.
context: Bottles and formula tried for a fussy two-month-old, UK.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Everything has been SO hard and expensive and it’s to be expected with a baby but still I just feel crap because I’m not enjoying this and I really thought I would be as he’s my last child.
context: Second child, also had a hard start with the first.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I did instantly think ‘tongue tie’ but was dismissed by the midwives and told that he could just be figuring out how to actually drink from a bottle.
context: Early feeding sounds she flagged in the first weeks.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: there’s been a heatwave over where we live for the past idek how long and he refuses to sleep in anything but long sleeved pyjama sets? The room is like a sauna and is easily around 27-30 degrees
context: Worried about overheating during a summer heatwave.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I just had a baby two weeks ago and I have a 16 month at home. I honestly don’t know how to keep my toddler entertained
context: Two under two, husband's leave ending.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My husband’s last week is this week with me. I’m upset for him not taking the whole 6 weeks of paid leave either to help.
context: Two weeks after her second birth, toddler at home.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I feel awful because I was pregnant for half the summer as well so I really struggled with keeping her entertained.
context: Guilt about the toddler's summer.

speaker: new_mother
quote: I got really used to him being with me and helping me with our newborn. I’m terrified of how I’m going to do it now that he’s going back to work.
context: One month after the birth, the night before her husband returns to work.

speaker: new_mother
quote: My husband and I usually do our shifts (he takes baby 7 pm to 1 am and then I take over 1 am to 8 am).
context: The night split they used during his leave.

speaker: new_mother
quote: He works 7 am to 3:30 pm so he would have to get up at 5 am and leave at 6:15 to commute to work.
context: Why the night shifts can't continue after his leave.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My husband is carrying all the weight. I’m burnt out, he’s burnt out, but we have a 4 year old so we must keep going.
context: Very sick in her second pregnancy, no help nearby.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: We don’t have any village either, it’s just him and I. Things didn’t feel this impossible before I got pregnant and sick. I feel like the worst mom and wife. I’m scared he will regret everything.
context: Second pregnancy with a four-year-old.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: how can a home test claim 99% accuracy, what all does that entail to market it?
context: First pregnancy, 7-8 weeks; an at-home sex test gave a result she hoped was wrong.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: it will just take adjusting to welcoming a boy when I’ve imagined, dreamed and desperately wanted a girl.
context: After a home sex test, first pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: at the end of the day I went to the bathroom and was looking at it and feeling around and what do you know… colostrum started leaking out!! I know this is very normal but I was not expecting it yet and for some reason this was the moment that altered my brain.
context: Almost 20 weeks, first pregnancy, noticed at work.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Ladies.. How do you come to terms with the fact your body is changing forever.
context: Shocked by an early body change at 20 weeks.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m disappointed that all the prep I did in order to not have no tears, to learn how to push where for nothing.
context: Told a surgical birth is needed; first baby.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: This sounds so silly but I hate the fact I’ll be paying for a surgeons honoraries.
context: Reacting to news of a planned surgical birth.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Honestly, I’m not really scared of passing out anymore. My biggest fear is going through the whole thing and then finding out they didn’t get enough blood for the testing and I have to repeat it.
context: Faints at blood draws; first labs coming up.

speaker: parent_unspecified
quote: I feel like I wake up just to eat and pee and then have to go back to bed until at least noon most days. My appointments exhaust me
context: 35 weeks, final month.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: But now, I’ve been asked four times by three separate family members if my toddler can attend the wedding without my husband and I. “Oh it’ll give you both time to acclimate to the new baby”
context: Due two days before her brother's out-of-state wedding.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: “She deserves to be able to go, we can watch her”  she still Cosleeps with us and the one time she slept without us she woke up in a panic and was inconsolable by anyone but me.
context: Family pushing to take her toddler to a wedding at the birth.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: AND on top of all of that, she deserves to be here when we bring home the baby, and thereafter. She deserves the time to acclimate and be around her younger sibling and bond with them.
context: Why she refuses to send her toddler away at the birth.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I need help deriving a kind but stern text that tells everyone in my family to stop asking me and that I am not comfortable with her going.
context: Asking strangers for wording to send her family.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: We have multiple people around us willing to help while I’m in labor […] But a baby is a big change for a toddler as is, and I don’t want my child feeling like she’s been replaced if she leaves for a week and comes home to a new sibling and new rules.
context: She already has labour-day help lined up for her toddler.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: my sister told me she doesn’t believe that my toddler has the ability to think like that?!?!
context: Her sister's response to her worry the toddler would feel replaced.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: my mother has spent so long asking me about grandkids and checking up on my reproductive health that it feels like admitting defeat to tell her that I'm pregnant.
context: Positive test after three years of trying.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I feel like all the other anecdotes I've heard have been so extreme one way or the other, I \*should\* be feeling more...something.
context: Newly pregnant and feeling calm rather than elated.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’ve had to take time off from my new job since falling pregnant and I’ve felt so ashamed and worried what people will think. I have felt embarrassed explaining how bad it’s been throughout the first trimester as every woman goes through it.
context: Back to work tomorrow after weeks off sick.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I look back at me throwing up 6 plus times a day, keeping absolutely no fluids down nor food. Completely repulsed by any food or drink. Exhaustion to the point my bones hurt even after sleeping.
context: End of her first trimester.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I can afford everything I need and then some for this baby, I am more than happy to buy everything well tbh I didnt get to with my first because we werent as financially fortunate and everything was hand me downs the first year !
context: Her friend keeps bringing items from free baby drives she doesn't need.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I would still do most things from marketplaces and I did buy one baby package from vinted… as the clothes I got given are … not our style. And as this will be our last baby I would like to dress him how we like this time around.
context: Buying for her last baby.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Lmao as I’m typing this I get a facebook notification that shes tagged me in another baby drive shes going to 🙃🙃🙃  knowing that the only thing I need are diapers as of right now
context: Friend keeps collecting free baby items for her.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: the doctors I spoke to seemed to really be trying to prepare me for the worst possible, saying 1 in 4 don’t work out.
context: 6+5 weeks, mild spotting; waiting days for blood results. Same post also in r/pregnant.
